title: What Happens If You Fall Into a Black Hole?

lines.text: What happens if you fall into a black hole? It depends on how big it is.
A small one, ten times as heavy as the Sun, pulls much harder on your feet than on your head.
You'd be stretched into a noodle before you even reach it. Astronomers really call this spaghettification.
A giant one, like the one at the center of our galaxy, is gentler. You'd cross its edge, the event horizon, and feel nothing.
But a friend watching from far away sees you slow down, turn red and fade, as if frozen at the edge.
For you, time goes on. Inside, every path leads to the center, and you have only seconds left.
What happens there? Nobody knows. Our laws of physics break down.
So if you get the choice, pick a giant one. Or better: be the friend.
